items.q: Who really controls muscle growth and strength?
items.a: The **nervous system** — upper motor neurons for deliberate effort, lower motor neurons releasing acetylcholine for contraction, and **central pattern generators** for rhythmic movement. Adaptation happens **after training**, not during it.

items.q: Do you need heavy weights to build muscle?
items.a: No. **Henneman's size principle** recruits motor units from low to high threshold, so **30–80% of 1RM** is enough for most strength and hypertrophy. Extreme strength may still need heavier loads.

items.q: How should strength and hypertrophy training feel different?
items.a: **Strength** = move load as a whole-body system with progressive overload. **Hypertrophy** = isolate hard local contractions (**mind-muscle intentionality**). Better isolation means fewer sets needed.

items.q: How many sets per muscle per week do you need?
items.a: **≥5 sets/week** at 30–80% 1RM just to **maintain**; **5–15 sets** to improve; advanced trainees can push **25–30** if recovery allows.

items.q: How often should you train to failure?
items.a: Only about **~10% of sets** to failure (**eighty-twenty exercise rule**). Keep most volume **sub-maximal** so you can still accumulate enough weekly work.

items.q: What rest intervals should you use between sets?
items.a: About **2 minutes** for Duncan French–style testosterone protocol work; **2–6 minutes** for hypertrophy and strength sets. Explosiveness work sits around **60–75% 1RM** with a fast concentric.

items.q: How can you check recovery for free each morning?
items.a: **Grip strength** drop of **≥10–20%** signals systemic nerve-to-muscle fatigue. **CO2 discard rate**: under **25–30 s** = not recovered; **30–60 s** = green zone; **65–120 s** = nervous system ready.

items.q: Why avoid ice baths and NSAIDs right around lifting?
items.a: Post-lift **ice baths** and **NSAIDs within ±4 hours** blunt inflammation-driven repair via the **mTOR pathway**, short-circuiting the gains you just trained for.

items.q: Which supplements and nutrients matter most here?
items.a: **Salt/electrolytes** enable nerve firing; **creatine monohydrate ~5 g/day** (studies show **12–20%** power gains); **leucine** from protein-dense meals (**700–3,000 mg** per meal, roughly **2–4 meals/day**).
